name: pk_to_sk_bridge_word

phase_0.boundary_condition: The secp256k1 elliptic curve group: generator G, order n, field prime p. The word encodes both the scalar (sk) and the point (pk) grammatically. The boundary closes when sk × G = pk is verified.

VINIT.justification: The void before the 64-glyph word is presented to the interpreter — no frame has been selected, no key exists.

TANCH.justification: The secp256k1 curve parameters (p, G, n) form the terminal anchor — all interpretations must satisfy the curve law.

AFWD.justification: Forward morphism: interpret the word as a public key point via bg-tuple frame. Scalar multiplication sk×G→pk is the forward direction.

AREV.justification: Reverse morphism: interpret the word as a private key scalar via hqe-tuple frame. Parity reversal changes the grammatical frame from pk to sk.

CLINK.justification: Sequential composition: the bridge word composes with the 64-glyph word, chaining the frame-change operation onto the encoded key pair.

IMSCRIB.justification: The word is self-referential: it IS both the public key and the private key simultaneously. The grammar's identity operator recognizes this dialetheic nature.

FSPLIT.justification: The word splits into two interpretive frames: the T-arm carries the pk-frame (bg-tuple interpretation), the F-arm carries the sk-frame (hqe-tuple interpretation with scalar extraction).

FFUSE.justification: The two frames reconstitute the original word: the pk-frame and sk-frame are dual aspects of the same grammatical object. FFUSE(FSPLIT(word)) = word holds because the word IS primally both.

EVALT.justification: Affirmative branch: the extracted scalar, when multiplied by G, yields the known public key point. Verification succeeds.

EVALF.justification: Negative branch: the extracted scalar does not match the public key. Wrong frame or corrupted interpretation.

ENGAGR.justification: The paradice: the word IS simultaneously the public key AND the private key. Both frames are true at once — this is the Belnap B-state, the grammatical encoding of the ECDLP.

IFIX.justification: The extracted 256-bit scalar is permanently recorded. Once fixed, the private key is irrevocably committed — the extraction is complete.

phase_2.split_input: the 64-glyph IMASM word encoding both pk and sk
split_outputs: pk-frame: bg-tuple interpretation yielding public key point
sk-frame: hqe-tuple interpretation yielding private key scalar
phase_2.fuse_result: the 64-glyph IMASM word encoding both pk and sk

phase_3.void_description: Before the word is instantiated — no key pair exists, no frame is selected, the elliptic curve is unpopulated.
phase_3.true_description: The pk-frame interpretation succeeds: the word-as-public-key maps to a valid secp256k1 point. The extracted scalar, multiplied by G, yields this point.
phase_3.false_description: The sk-frame interpretation fails: the extracted scalar does not verify. Frame mismatch or the word does not encode a valid private key.
phase_3.both_description: The dialetheic state: the word IS simultaneously the public key and the private key. Both interpretations are true — this is the grammatical ECDLP, where sk and pk are dual aspects of one word.
